Conflicts with the three-state return table L106 + ladder L129, which map {groups: [], malformed: false} to "section absent entirely" -> rung 2. Per lib/parallel/groups.mjs:22-25, a zero-byte or whitespace-only file is read SUCCESSFULLY and returns exactly that state. The spec defines no rule anywhere distinguishing an fs-level throw from a successful empty read; Resource bounds L85 checks the size ceiling and regular-file, not zero length. A truncated-to-zero plan is therefore simultaneously rung 3 ("unreadable") and rung 2 ("absent"), and an attacker committing an empty plan chooses which false statement the brief asserts. Same one-fact-two-ways class as prior CON-1 and CON-2; escalated because it survived a revision specifically tasked with eliminating that class. FIX: state that rung 3 is entered only on an fs throw or a failed pre-read check, and that a successful read of any content (including empty) enters the parser and is classified by the three-state table - or give zero-length its own fourth state annotated "present but empty". Add a zero-byte fixture AC.

## security-reviewer:path-traversal:6fed7ac6

```yaml
blocker_id: security-reviewer:path-traversal:6fed7ac6
section_anchor: resource-bounds
reviewer_count: 1
```

**Reviewer:** security-reviewer

```
SEC-6 (NEW). The sibling containment rule resolves with path.resolve and compares against the canonicalized ROOT, never canonicalizing the CANDIDATE. path.resolve does not follow symlinks; stat does. A fork PR committing .context-index/specs/x/x.plan.md as a symlink to a CI runner file passes containment, passes the regular-file and 1 MiB checks, and is opened. This spec is the surface introducing symlink handling (Resource bounds argues about "a committed symlink to a character device"; AC L259 pins only symlink-to-non-regular-file), so canonicalize-then-recheck belongs here. Rung-3 annotations ("oversized" / "not a regular file" / "unreadable" / "absent") render to STDOUT in the public PR body, giving a per-path existence / file-type / size oracle over the runner filesystem, one symlink per commit; the sibling stderr-diagnostics rule does not cover them. FIX: require fs.realpath (or lstat + refusal to follow) on the candidate and re-assert containment under .context-index/specs/ AFTER canonicalization, before stat and before any read; a plan whose realpath escapes is never opened and renders the same annotation as any other out-of-bounds trailer, with no distinction between exists / wrong type / oversized. Add an AC. CWE-59, CWE-22.
```
